title: CKD-Mineral and Bone Disorder: Phosphate Binders, Vitamin D and FGF-23 Axis
subject: ss-paediatric-nephrology
module: Pediatric AKI, Dialysis and Chronic Kidney Disease

steps.say: Progressive nephron loss sets off an endocrine chain reaction disrupting mineral metabolism.
steps.tx: Trace the metabolic consequences driving the **Pathophysiological cascade of CKD-MBD** as renal clearance deteriorates. Declining GFR causes systemic phosphate retention, triggering osteocyte secretion of FGF-23 and downregulating renal 1-alpha-hydroxylase (CYP27B1), leading to 1,25(OH)2D deficiency, resultant hypocalcemia, and progressive secondary hyperparathyroidism that damages the developing pediatric skeleton.

steps.say: Circulating parathyroid hormone requires intentional permissive elevation to overcome skeletal resistance.
steps.tx: Calibrate mineral management targeting established **Stage-based serum PTH target ranges** in progressive kidney disease. KDIGO recommends maintaining intact PTH at 1.5-3x upper normal limit in CKD Stage 4 (70-150 pg/mL) and 2-9x upper normal limit in CKD Stage 5 / dialysis (150-300 pg/mL) to avoid adynamic bone disease caused by excessive parathyroid suppression.

vis.title: Target Intact PTH Ranges by CKD Stage

steps.say: Enteric phosphate binders block absorption and must be matched to patient calcium dynamics.
steps.tx: Prescribe mealtime enteric binding using customized **Phosphate binder selection in children** according to calcemia. Calcium-based binders like calcium carbonate or calcium acetate are ingested with meals to bind dietary phosphate; non-calcium binders such as sevelamer carbonate at 50-100 mg/kg/day are preferred if hypercalcemia, hyperphosphatemia, or early vascular calcification develops.

left.title: Calcium-Based Binders
points: Taken strictly with meals to bind phosphate
Risk of hypercalcemia and vascular calcification

right.title: Non-Calcium Binders
points: Preferred in hypercalcemia or elevated calcium-phosphate product
Does not contribute to systemic elemental calcium load

steps.say: Activated vitamin D suppresses parathyroid transcription but requires strict safety thresholds.
steps.tx: Administer active sterols following protocolized **Active vitamin D analog dosing** with biochemical oversight. Active vitamin D sterols like oral calcitriol at 0.25-1 mcg/day or alfacalcidol directly suppress parathyroid PTH gene expression; therapy must be paused if serum calcium x phosphate product exceeds 55-65 mg²/dL² to prevent severe metastatic soft-tissue and cardiovascular calcification.

vis.title: Active Vitamin D Regimen Safety Parameters
rows: Titrate to intact PTH target range
Pause if Ca x P > 55-65 mg²/dL²

steps.say: Allosteric receptor activators overcome refractory parathormone excess in hemodialysis patients.
steps.tx: Control refractory severe secondary hyperparathyroidism by initiating **Calcimimetic agents in pediatric dialysis** under monitoring. Cinacalcet, an oral allosteric modulator of the calcium-sensing receptor, or intravenous etelcalcetide is utilized in adolescent patients maintained on long-term hemodialysis with severe secondary hyperparathyroidism refractory to active vitamin D sterols, lowering parathormone without increasing serum calcium or phosphate.

nodes.label: Severe Refractory Secondary HPT on HD

steps.say: Excessive suppression freezes skeletal remodeling and causes dangerous mineral deposition in vascular walls.
steps.tx: Prevent iatrogenic skeletal paralysis by recognizing critical **Adynamic bone disease risks** during aggressive treatment. Over-suppression of PTH to an intact PTH < 100 pg/mL produces adynamic bone disease characterized by absent bone turnover, osteomalacia, loss of skeletal capacity to buffer postprandial calcium loads, and severe accelerated metastatic arterial and cardiac valvular calcification.

left.title: High-Turnover Bone Disease
points: Elevated bone resorption and fibrous replacement
Marrow fibrosis with marrow space distortion

right.title: Adynamic Bone Disease
points: Acellular bone surfaces without osteoid seams
Inability to buffer postprandial mineral shifts

steps.say: Growing growth plates subjected to metabolic stress develop painful and disabling physical deformities.
steps.tx: Examine growing long bones diligently to identify **Skeletal deformities in growing children** with chronic uremia. Renal osteodystrophy in pediatric patients uniquely produces slipped capital femoral epiphysis (SCFE), marked genu valgum (knock-knees), progressive metaphyseal cupping and fraying on radiographs, and prominent rachitic rosary costochondral beading along the anterior chest wall.

vis.title: Pediatric Renal Osteodystrophy Physical Manifestations
rows: Hip or knee pain with limp and external rotation
Knock-knee angular deformity during growth spurt
Radiographic widening and fraying of growth plate
Palpable expansion of anterior thoracic ribs

steps.say: Dietary restriction halts early phosphate accumulation before skeletal damage becomes permanent.
steps.tx: Implement nutritional intake modifications applying **Dietary phosphorus restriction guidelines** early in chronic kidney disease. Dietary phosphate restriction to 100% of Dietary Reference Intake (DRI) for age is initiated as soon as intact PTH rises above baseline normative ranges, strictly eliminating processed convenience foods, dark sodas, and preserved meats rich in highly bioavailable inorganic phosphate additives.

nodes.label: PTH Rises Above Upper Normal Threshold
Restrict Phosphorus to 100% DRI for Age
Maintain Normal Phosphate & Retard Bone Disease
